guidebook.intro: Time and days. Weekdays in this course are numbered: **Etu alu** (day one) is Monday, up to **Etu azya** (Saturday); Sunday is **Sabiti**.

tips.title: Ndrani, drusi, ndrozi
body: **Ndrani** today, **drusi** tomorrow, **ndrozi** yesterday. **Ngaa** is morning, **etu ti** afternoon, **ondre** evening and **ini** night.
**Etu dria** is every day: **dria** (all) follows the noun.

tips.title: Sawa ngbe?
body: **Sawa ngbe?** asks the time. Hours are counted from sunrise, as in Swahili: **sawa alu** (hour one) is seven o’clock, **sawa su** ten o’clock.
Half past is **ka nusu**: **sawa na ka nusu** (half past nine).

culture.title: East African time
body: Counting hours from six in the morning is common across East Africa; check whether someone means clock time or local time.
